subject: Meteorology
title: Tornado Outbreaks
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Tornado Outbreaks.

hook.text: A tornado outbreak produces many tornadoes in a short period—sometimes dozens across multiple states.

buildup.text: Outbreaks occur when a powerful weather system combines extreme instability, moisture, and strong wind shear.

discovery.text: The Super Outbreak of April 2011 spawned 362 tornadoes in three days—including four rated EF5.

twist.text: The 1974 Super Outbreak was thought unbeatable with 148 tornadoes—2011 more than doubled that record.

climax.text: Outbreaks are forecast days in advance using ensemble models—but which individual storms will tornado remains uncertain.

punchline.text: We can predict the outbreak—but not exactly which storm spins.

quiz.question: How many tornadoes did the 2011 Super Outbreak produce?
